cards.back: Trust, one-click verification, audit months later, and the cheapest hallucination signal: a sentence whose citation fails a check.
You can only cite what you labelled: store a stable id and source metadata with every chunk. If re-chunking changes ids, old citations break.
Document, page or section, chunk, span (quote) and table cell or XBRL fact. Finer grains are easier to check but can hide context.
Pass documents with citations enabled; the provider guarantees the quoted text is in the document. The highest-trust approach.
Writing first and then searching for a similar source nearly always finds something, but sharing words is not supporting the claim.
The cited id was retrieved, the quote is in the source, and every number in the sentence is in the source.
An NLI model or LLM judge reads (source, sentence) and answers supported, contradicted or not enough information. It catches laundering.
When a sentence fails, drop it, regenerate it or say the source doesn't state it. Don't show it with a warning.
A real citation attached to a claim it doesn't support, like "operating margin improved [c41]" when c41 is about gross margin. Only entailment catches it.
Recall: share of sentences fully supported by their citations. Precision: share of individual citations that support their sentence; over-citing lowers it.
In production, the share of sentences the verifier dropped or flagged. A rise after a change is a regression alarm that needs no labels.

cards.front: Never use list positions as ids
cards.back: "doc 3" changes whenever ranking does; use stable chunk ids.

quiz.q: The model cites c77, which was never retrieved. What catches it?
quiz.why: Checking ids against the retrieved set is exact and free.

quiz.q: "Operating margin improved [c41]", but c41 is about gross margin. What catches it?
quiz.why: The id and quote are real; only an entailment check sees the claim isn't supported.

quiz.q: Which way of getting citations from a model is lowest trust?
quiz.why: Markers need regex parsing and list positions change when ranking does.

quiz.q: A computed operating margin of 29.8% appears in the answer. What should it cite?
choices: Nothing; computed numbers need no source
quiz.why: Every number must come from a cited chunk or a calculator output.

quiz.q: A sentence fails verification. What should happen?
choices: Show it with a warning icon
Ask the user to check it

quiz.q: Adding three ids to a sentence that one supports lowers which metric?
quiz.why: Precision counts how many individual citations support their sentence.

quiz.q: Why do citations depend on ingestion?
choices: Citations are generated at indexing time
You can only cite ids and metadata stored with each chunk
quiz.why: Stable ids and source metadata must be written with every chunk.
